findings.title: Avoid calculating a filtered cache that constant motion vectors discard next frame
findings.repro: Above the reference area, run a preset with constant mv_a > 0 and positive vector counts. Every frame after the first draws new vectors, forcing MRT before the warp. The final MRT again calculates a filtered image, then the next frame draws vectors and recomputes it before use.
findings.impact: Two 3/4-tap stencil calculations run every frame, although only the input calculation is consumed by the warp. Equal fullscreen pass counts do not establish equal fetch/write work or GPU frame rate.
findings.suggestion: Use an exact raw-only output path when appropriate and invalidate the filtered cache, or otherwise avoid calculating this unused filtered output. Validate motion-vector appearance and cache transitions, then measure device cost.

findings.title: Avoid retaining the unused legacy flip surface alongside the MRT raw copy
findings.repro: Switch to a diffusion-eligible preset at 4K. ProjectM::StartPresetTransition calls DrawInitialImage. CopyTexture::Draw allocates a full-size flip texture and swaps image attachments. The active path then allocates its own raw and filtered MRT textures; the old flip remains alive until the inactive or fallback path needs it.
findings.evidence: ProjectM.cpp StartPresetTransition; CopyTexture.cpp Draw(Framebuffer&) and UpdateTextureSize; patch lines 260–261, 548–560 and 585–590.
findings.impact: One redundant live RGBA8 surface occupies 31.64 MiB at 4K per active preset. The 48 MiB texture-pool limit covers discarded textures, not these live attachments. This does not establish an out-of-memory failure or a GPU frame-rate change.
findings.suggestion: Reuse the existing flip attachment as the MRT raw target, or provide careful release/recreation ownership when entering or leaving the active path. Test initial-image, resize, fallback and inactive transitions.

findings.title: Correct the RGB and opaque-alpha test comment
findings.repro: Trace the two default CreateColorAttachment calls to Framebuffer.cpp lines 220–222: both create RGBA/unsigned-byte attachments. The MRT shader copies all four source channels.
findings.impact: The false format claim misleads alpha-cause and memory analysis. This test does not assert that readback alpha is opaque.
findings.suggestion: Describe the actual RGBA storage and alpha behavior. Preserve historical evidence with an explicit erratum rather than reinterpreting past results.

inactive_contract: Construction creates a program, FBO and zero-size attachment objects. Pixel storage is allocated by active Draw.SetSize. After an active episode, both MRT surfaces remain live while inactive: the reference guard avoids draws but does not free prior storage. This is a bounded cache tradeoff, not unbounded growth.
residual_risks: GPU frame-rate, thermal and bandwidth acceptance remain unmeasured.
The existing pool counts RGBA16F as eight bytes per pixel and counts mip levels, but its limit does not cap live memory.
These findings address immutable patch 0033. The owner adapted preset member context in 0036; the final revision needs its own review.
testing_gaps: Account for cached-output consumption and invalidation with continuous motion vectors.
Track live texture attachments across preset load, active-to-inactive changes, resizing and memory pressure.
Verify mixed RGBA8/RGBA16F framebuffer completeness on the actual diagnostic target.
